newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kabila may ask S.Africa to hand over Mobutu men.
newsitem.headline: Kabila may ask S.Africa to hand over Mobutu men.

text.p: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, has told South Africa it may ask for some of former president Mobutu Sese Seko's allies to be extradited, a Sunday newspaper reported.

"...They broadly said that they would have to review everyone who is in the country (South Africa) with the objective of seeing whether there could be extradition agreements," South Africa's deputy foreign minister Aziz Pahad told The Sunday Independent.
He added that several countries had been requested for extradition agreements. Foreign ministry officials were not available for comment.

"The general feeling is that there has been some misuse of funds," Pahad said, but added that the Congo's new leader Laurent Kabila had not directly raised the issue of money and assets that may have been smuggled out of his country to South Africa.
Several high-profile members of Mobutu's inner circle are believed to be in South Africa.

The paper said Mobutu's son Kongolo owned property in the northern suburbs of Johannesburg, but was thought to be with his ailing father in Morocco. Also believed to be in South Africa was Mobutu's former chief of staff General Baramoto Kapama.
Many of the Zairean refugees own property in Johannesburg's plusher suburbs and at least one owns a house on Cape Town's expensive Atlantic coast.

South Africa's deputy minister of Intelligence Services Joe Nhlanhla told the newspaper his department was investigating which Zaireans fled to South Africa in the midst of the civil war, and which had residence permits from before.
He said they were also investigating the circumstances surrounding the issue of these permits.
